entries.text: What, does that last forever? Forty years ago, I drove down to the city hall, down to the hall of records. Record archives, whatever they call it. I wanted to look up my wife. It... Bothered me I couldn't remember her name. Love lasts... Seventy-five years, if you're lucky. You don't want to be around when it's gone. Count your blessings.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: Why are you this way? I mean, if this is true, give me something in the way of proof. Help me find some science that I can hang this on.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: It has nothing to do with science. Someone took my place.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: Took your place?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I don't know her name. I don't think I ever knew it. I had yellow fever way the hell back then... When it killed half of new york. Washington square park was a common grave, they had so many bodies. They'd bury them shallow. They wrapped them in yellow sheets, and the yellow sheets would stick up through the mud. I was in a city-run contagion ward. I was out of my head with fever, out of my mind, then I saw him-- saw death. Wish I would've had a camera then. At first, I... Just saw him out of the corner of my eye. Then he got bolder and he started flitting around the room, and he'd take this person and he'd take that person. And I never saw his face. I didn't want to see his face. I figured if I saw it, he'd take me too.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: But he didn't.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: No. There was a nurse. She did the best she could. Back then, medical science was-- they couldn't find their ass with both hands. They still can't. But she did the best she could. She sat with me. Held my hand. I was on my deathbed, then he came for me. I didn't look at him. I closed my eyes and turned my head. I didn't tell her not to look at him. I wanted her to look at him. I wanted her to look at him instead of me. And then I came to and the fever broke. They were carrying her out wrapped up in a yellow sheet. Since that time, I realized you got to be careful what you wish for. I missed my chance. You're very lucky, you know that?
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: What do you mean? Wait a minute. Say what's on your mind. You mean lucky like the others? You want me to believe that I'm about to die?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I just want to take the picture.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: You took my picture. You took my picture last night. Is this why?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: No. That was different.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: I'm not gonna die!
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: [ charging ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Turn that off.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: No.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: Turn it off right now! Put it down!
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: There is nothing to be done for it.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: You took my phone. Why?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Please, just give me a chance.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: What don't you want me to know?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: He's coming. He's coming, and you should just make your peace.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: Shut up!
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: [ door crashes open ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: He's here.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: [ flashbulb charging ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Agent? Oh, god. Don't. No, no, no, no, no. Come on, come on. Damn it! I'll get help. We need some help in here!
entries.speaker: Agent Ritter

entries.text: Do you see him? Do you see him? Don't look. Close your eyes.
entries.speaker: Alfred Fellig

entries.text: You're a lucky man. Coroner's report came back on Fellig. Says he died of a single gunshot wound. That's all it said. Well, I, uh, talked to your doctor, and he says you're doing great. You're making the fastest recovery he's ever seen.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: You know, Mulder, I don't even know how I entertained the thought. People don't live forever.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: No, I-I think he would have. I just think that death only looks for you... Once you seek its opposite.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder
